_readme: Scenario data for the Scenario tab. Add a scenario by appending to `scenarios`; add a map node to `nodes`. Positions are illustrative. Step fields: title, text, before (optional 'today' contrast), reqs, mo, stages (nine-stage keys), show (node ids on the map), links ([from, to, kind] with kind up|down|two|cue|relay), focus (node ids to frame), latency ({leg, segments}), area (show the S3-06 geo-target footprint), interfaces ([{id, note}]), note (optional caveat).

scenarios.title: Flood warning chain
scenarios.summary: A gauge on the Ubangi crosses its threshold. S-3 gets the message out, the agency authorizes a warning, S-3 broadcasts it in the local language, confirms delivery, and carries the response.

steps.title: Trigger
steps.text: A river gauge on the Ubangi, under heavy rain and canopy, crosses its flood threshold.
steps.before: Today this reading would sit unreported. Only 13-15 of 400+ pre-1960 river stations still operate, few in real time, and sensors sync only after 3-7 days.

steps.title: Uplink (BASINLINK)
steps.text: The gauge sends a priority message straight to the S-3 space segment, from under the canopy.

steps.title: Ground and COP
steps.text: The message is relayed to a gateway and appears in the common operating picture (COP). The COP cues S-1 to revisit the reach.

interfaces.note: COP cues an S-1 revisit of the priority area.

steps.title: Authority decision
steps.text: The national agency reviews the data and authorizes the alert. S-3 does not decide. The alert arrives at S-3 as a CAP message.
steps.note: The S3-05 clock starts when the alert is authorized, so the agency’s decision time is outside S-3’s budget.

steps.title: Broadcast (BASINCAST)
steps.text: The alert is geo-targeted to the reach at risk, spoken in the local language, and broadcast to community receivers.

steps.title: Confirmation
steps.text: Delivery confirmation returns to the agency. The agency knows which receivers played the alert. This closes MO-2.

steps.title: Response coordination
steps.text: Two-way terminals carry commands and acknowledgments to rangers and responders. A-2 confirms the situation overhead and A-3 is dispatched.

interfaces.note: A-2’s ≤45 min clock starts when our alert is delivered.
Dispatch commands and acknowledgments over two-way terminals.

scenarios.title: Routine collection
scenarios.summary: Thousands of gauges, wildlife tags, ranger devices and A-4 balloons send small daily payloads from under the canopy, across the whole basin.

steps.title: Terminals across the basin
steps.text: Low-power terminals sit on gauges, wildlife tags and ranger devices, under canopy, everywhere in the basin.
steps.before: Today sensors and ranger devices sync only after 3-7 days.

steps.title: Daily payloads
steps.text: Each terminal sends its routine daily data. The constellation serves every terminal in the basin.

steps.title: A-4 balloons ride the same link
steps.text: A-4 balloon and sonde payloads uplink through BASINLINK like any other terminal.

interfaces.note: Balloon and sonde payloads uplink through BASINLINK.

steps.title: Into the COP
steps.text: Everything lands in the COP through the gateway. Terminals run for years on solar or battery.

scenarios.title: Degraded operations
scenarios.pov: Responders after towers and grid fail
scenarios.summary: Conflict or storms take out towers and the grid. Rangers and responders keep working over S-3 two-way terminals, and A-1 and S-3 cover for each other.

steps.title: Terrestrial networks go down
steps.text: Conflict or storms take out cell towers and the grid around the response area.
steps.before: Floods and conflict take down towers and the grid, and internet reaches only about 27-32% of people even before that.

steps.title: Two-way over S-3
steps.text: Rangers and responders switch to S-3 two-way terminals. Commands go out and acknowledgments come back.

steps.title: A-1 relay as a complement
steps.text: Where A-1 is on station, it adds a regional relay. S-3 stays the primary basin-wide layer, and each covers for the other.

interfaces.note: Complementary regional relay. Overlap on “comms lost in conflict”, TBR with the A-1 team.

steps.note: S-3 primary, A-1 complementary is our assumption, TBR with the A-1 team.

steps.title: Service holds through the weather
steps.text: Availability is specified in heavy tropical rain, so the link is sized for the weather that drives floods in the first place.

scenarios.title: Non-flood hazard
scenarios.summary: S-2 detects disturbance under the canopy, the alert reaches rangers, A-2 confirms overhead, and S-3 carries the two-way link. The same comms layer serves every hazard.

steps.title: S-2 detects disturbance
steps.text: S-2 sees new clearing under the canopy in the Sangha forest and flags it to the COP.

interfaces.note: Detections become alerts and tasking that S-3 carries to rangers.

steps.title: Alert reaches rangers
steps.text: The responsible agency authorizes an alert. S-3 geo-targets it to the rangers covering that area.

steps.title: A-2 confirms overhead
steps.text: A-2 launches from its dock and confirms the incursion from overhead, reporting back over S-3.

interfaces.note: A-2’s ≤45 min clock starts when our alert is delivered.

steps.title: Two-way link for the response
steps.text: Rangers move with S-3 two-way terminals: commands out, acknowledgments back. The same layer that carried the flood warning carries this.
